01/26/2024
Claim received from the insured's side for a sideswipe that occurred while the other vehicle was changing lanes. The
claimant reports a knee injury and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will route through the attorney's
office.
03/12/2024
Reviewed the first notice of loss and the description of the lane change. The account is consistent with the damage
pattern noted on the intake form.
03/27/2024
Police report obtained. It places the claimant's vehicle in the affected lane at the time of ipmact and records
statements from the responding officer that match the reported sequence.
05/01/2024
Photos of both vehicles received. The dmaage to the claimant's rear quarter paenl and door lines up with the contact
area described by the other driver.
05/05/2024
Spoke with the other driver, who gave the same accuont of the lane change as in the first notice. Confirmed the driver
is listed on the policy and that coverage was in force on the loss date with no lapse.
05/12/2024
Two independent witnesses were interviewed. Both confirm the sideswipe happened as described and that the
claimant was seated in the vehicle throughout.
05/20/2024
Appraisal of the vehicle is complete. The repair scope fits the impact described, and no prior damage to this vehicle
appears in our records or in the inspection notes.
05/31/2024
Medical records received from the claimant's treating provider. The knee injury is a plausible result of a collision of
this type, and the initial treatment followed a standard course.
07/11/2024
Prior records show a minor strain in the same knee area several years ago, which resolved completely with no
ongoing complaints noted at the time.
08/11/2024
Claimant's account has been consistent across every conversation, including the recorded statement taken through
counsel. No changes to the sequence of events have been raised.
08/18/2024
Treatment frequency has tapered as the claimant's condition improved, with follow-up visits now spaced out and
discharge expected based on the current notes.
09/11/2024
File is ready for evaluation of the injury and property damage components. Coordinating with counsel on the bodily
injury demand and the repair authorization.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
